# Strategic ICP: Ledgerline

The ideal customer is a mid-sized distributor with several legal entities and a small finance team that can no longer keep up with supplier invoices.

## Blocking Unknowns

None

## 5. Buyer Situations

| ID | Situation | Trigger | Already tried | Deciding between | Stage weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Close keeps slipping | Month-end ran late twice | Overtime | Hire or automate | Learn 40%, Problem 40%, Buy 20% |
| S2 | Outgrew the spreadsheet | A duplicate payment | A shared sheet | Tool or service | Learn 20%, Problem 30%, Buy 50% |
| S3 | New entity added | An acquisition | The ERP module | Extend ERP or add a tool | Learn 10%, Problem 40%, Buy 50% |

## 6. Alternatives

| Category | Named examples | Why buyers pick it | Why they leave or avoid it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | Not named in the inputs | No cost | The backlog grows |
| Self-serve software | PayStack Pro (free plan; paid from $40/month); Tallyo (free options, paid tiers) | Cheap | Still manual |
| Outsourced service | Northbook (monthly retainer plus a fee per entity; claims 3,000 clients and a 20,000-invoice daily capacity) | Hands-off | Slow answers |
| ERP module | Corevia (pricing not published) | Already owned | Clumsy |
